newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December S&P 500 futures finish higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December S&P 500 futures finish higher.

text.p: U.S. December Standard and Poor's 500 futures finished higher after a very choppy session caught between T-bond strength and profit-taking.
Traders said interest most of the day was fickle on both sides of the market.

Stock index futures rallied early with Treasury bond futures after bullish economic data, then collapsed into negative territory to hit a fresh session low at midday. Traders said midday profit-taking and nervousness amid this week's data lineup kept buyers wary. But T-bond strength was unrelenting, feeding an afternoon S&P recovery, traders said.
December S&Ps drifted off their highs after Treasury bond futures closed, only to charge back near the session's peak before the close.
Traders said stop-loss orders were hit on both sides of the market at several times during the session.
"It was pretty choppy this afternoon and it's a big tug of war," an S&P 500 futures trader said.
"We took out what we thought was going to be a key area at 706.80 and we didn't get much followthrough at 707.00 and we had a nasty little selloff after the bonds closed," the trader said.
"But then they closed on a strong note still," he said. "I don't know what to make of it."
Others said the strong close could mean another leg up in this bull market.

"We've seen such lousy closes recently that this bodes well," said George Roth, order manager for Cargill Investor Services in the S&P pit. "Any followthrough in the bonds tomorrow leads to euphoria over here too," he said.
A weaker than expected third-quarter employment price index sparked the early T-bond rally, and a drop in October consumer confidence continued the bullish mood.

December T-bonds soared through a seven-month high at key resistance of 111-28/32 and nearly retraced 50 percent of their 9-1/2 month downmove. The T-bond strength kept S&P 500s buoyant much of the day, traders said, but profit-taking kept cutting gains.
Third-quarter preliminary U.S. growth, forecast at 1.8 percent, was due on Wednesday, along with September new home sales and the Fed's beige book of economic activity.
On Friday, October employment data will be released. Jobs were forecast up 212,000 compared with a 40,000 September decline. The unemployment rate was seen steady at 5.2 percent.

December S&Ps settled up 5.90 points at 706.25, Value Lines rose 1.10 points to 643.10, Nikkei 225 rose 85.0 to 20,965.0, Midcap 400s lost 0.45 to 242.20, and NYSE Composite rose 3.15 points to 375.40. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
